abstract: An LLM agent’s cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company’s Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.7% and raises its pass rate by 14.34%. The same environment transfers to Opus 5, cutting its cost by 68.1% with a 1.34% gain. Added on top of Meta-Harness’s optimized harness for Haiku 4.5, it lowers cost by a further 83.4% and adds 11.17% accuracy over Meta-Harness alone. Across 5 benchmarks, EnvOpt significantly reduces the cost of agents while improving or maintaining pass rate, and is transferable to different models and different harnesses. We also discuss common successful and rejected environment optimization strategies during automated optimization. More broadly, our results show that how information is represented to an agent shapes both its cost and its success, making the environment worth optimizing in addition to the parameters and the harness.

sections.body: An agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness and its environment, but the environment is usually treated as fixed. The paper proposes optimizing *stationary environments*, which are shared by many tasks. EnvOpt uses a coding agent to edit the environment representation for a target agent, using training tasks without verifiers. A validation set with verifiers tracks cost and pass rate. Across five benchmarks, EnvOpt reduces cost on unseen test sets by an average of 48%, with higher or similar pass rates. The authors also report transfer to other models and harnesses, and gains when combined with Meta-Harness.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Environment optimization is proposed as a third axis, alongside parameter tuning and harness optimization, for improving LLM agents.

sections.body: The research agent, a coding agent such as Codex, runs over several steps. At each step it receives a disjoint set of training tasks, the current environment directory and a budget. It runs the target agent, analyzes the trajectories and edits the environment to lower cost without hurting pass rate. It cannot modify the target harness. Verifiers for training tasks are hidden to prevent reward hacking, so the agent judges quality with proxies or answer consistency. After each step, the environment is run on a validation set. Evolution stops if validation cost increases or pass rate drops significantly, and the previous environment is kept.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: EnvOpt runs a research agent that edits the environment over disjoint training steps, stopping when validation cost rises.

sections.body:
- **AutomationBench:** 200 test tasks, 96 validation tasks and 20 training tasks per step, stopped at step 5. EnvOpt cuts cost by 72.7% and raises pass rate by 14.3%, with significantly better outcomes than GEPA and Meta-Harness on the same training pool.
- **Transfer:** an average cost reduction of 75.7% across other harnesses and models, including Opus 5.
- **Workspace-Bench:** 80 test and 20 validation tasks, with training tasks synthesized without verifiers. Cost falls by 47.65% and pass rate rises by 3.3%.
- **Data-Eng-Bench:** cost falls by 53.44% without hurting performance.
- **Meta-Harness combination:** EnvOpt further lowers cost for Haiku 4.5 and still improves pass rate for Opus 5.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: EnvOpt cuts Haiku 4.5 cost by 72.7% on AutomationBench and raises pass rate by 14.3%, and it transfers to other models.

sections.body: Successful edits included a program that presents Gmail as plain text, cheatsheets of API endpoints, a file index, an SQLite database, a file-ranking program for Bleve and a test validator for tenacity. Rejected edits included one large file of column values, which increased exploration, and a search tool that returned too many files. Most of the cost reduction came from input environment-feedback tokens. Tool-only optimization gave smaller gains than full optimization. An early SQL splitter flaw in Data-Eng-Bench stayed uncovered until step 5. Validation cost reduction correlated with tool call changes during training, with Pearson correlation of 0.75 on AutomationBench.
sections.heading: Discussion
sections.headline: Successful edits included converters, cheatsheets and databases, while oversized files and over-broad search tools raised cost.

sections.body: The paper defines environment optimization as a third direction alongside harness optimization and parameter tuning. EnvOpt, an automated research pipeline, reduces agent cost across five benchmarks while maintaining or improving success rates. The authors report transfer across models and harnesses, and outperformance over GEPA, Meta-Harness, gskill and advisor models. EnvOpt can also build on Meta-Harness to push the Pareto frontier further. Tool-only optimization performed worse than full optimization, and cost savings exceed 10 times the cost of running EnvOpt. Successful and rejected examples are offered as design guidance for future work.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Environment optimization is presented as a third direction that cuts agent cost while maintaining or improving success across five benchmarks.

sections.body: This appendix gives the instructions provided to the research agent on each of the five benchmarks in Section 3. The supplied section text contains only the heading for each benchmark: AutomationBench, Workspace-Bench, Data-Eng-Bench, Bleve and Tenacity. The instruction text itself is not present in the supplied section, so its contents cannot be summarized beyond these headings.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists research agent instructions for AutomationBench, Workspace-Bench, Data-Eng-Bench, Bleve and Tenacity.
